options.text: "Wait until you're sure they'll actually listen."
options.then: Aditi nods. "Maybe next month, then."

options.text: "For a serious offence, police must register an FIR."
options.then: Aditi looks up. "Must? They don't get to choose?"

options.text: "Honestly? Yeah, they probably will just send you away."
options.then: Aditi's shoulders drop. "Then why go at all?"

options.text: "Just post about it online instead. It's easier."
options.then: Aditi hesitates. "That feels even scarier."

steps.why: For a serious offence, registering an FIR isn't optional for police. It's not her fault.

steps.prompt: Aditi asks: "What if it didn't happen near that station?"

options.text: "Just tell them everything on 112 instead of going."
options.then: Aditi hesitates. "It's not an emergency right now, though."

options.text: "Then you have to travel to the right area first."
options.then: Aditi groans. "That's two hours away."

options.text: "A Zero FIR can be filed at any police station."
options.then: Aditi thinks. "So the nearest one is fine."

options.text: "Then they're allowed to refuse you. That's the rule."
options.then: Aditi looks deflated. "I knew it."

steps.why: A Zero FIR works at any station, so distance isn't a reason to give up.

steps.prompt: Aditi says: "I'm still scared to go alone."

options.text: "Then don't go. It's not worth all the stress."
options.then: Aditi nods, relieved and stuck at the same time.

options.text: "Take a trusted adult. I'll come too, if you want."
options.then: Aditi nods. "My aunt might come. And you."

options.text: "You'll be fine. They'll definitely catch him and punish him."
options.then: Aditi looks unsure. "You can't promise that."

options.text: "Go on your own. It shows them you're serious."
options.then: Aditi pales at the thought.

steps.why: A trusted adult beside her makes the route easier to use.

scenarios.relearn: FIR is mandatory for serious crimes; a Zero FIR can be filed anywhere.

scenarios.hook: Your younger brother Ishaan, 11, spots the helpline list on your fridge.
scenarios.setup: He's reading it over his breakfast.

steps.prompt: Ishaan asks: "Why do these numbers even matter?"

options.text: "They mean help is one call away, for you and for others."
options.then: Ishaan looks at the list again. "Which one's for kids?"

options.text: "Because the world is full of really dangerous people."
options.then: Ishaan's spoon stops. "Like who?"

options.text: "Don't worry about it. That's adult stuff, not kids' stuff."
options.then: Ishaan frowns. "But it's on our fridge."

options.text: "They don't, really. Nothing bad is going to happen."
options.then: Ishaan shrugs and goes back to his cereal.

steps.why: Knowing the numbers means help is close, without needing to be scared.

steps.prompt: Ishaan asks: "Which one would I call?"

options.text: "1930. That one works for absolutely anything, day or night."
options.then: Ishaan nods. "Okay, 1930 for everything."

options.text: "Only me. You won't ever need the numbers."
options.then: Ishaan nods. "What if you're away at college, though?"

options.text: "All of them, one after another, until somebody picks up."
options.then: Ishaan looks confused. "That's a lot of calling."

options.text: "Tell Mum or me. Or 1098 if you're unsafe, 112 in emergencies."
options.then: Ishaan counts on his fingers. "Mum, you, 1098, 112. Easy."

steps.why: A trusted adult, Childline 1098 and 112 are what a child most needs to know.

steps.prompt: Ishaan asks: "Can I tell my friend Zara about them?"

options.text: "No. Keep it in the family."
options.then: Ishaan looks puzzled. "Why's it a secret?"

options.text: "Yes. Sharing them helps keep her safe too."
options.then: Ishaan grins. "I'll tell her at lunch."

options.text: "Sure. Tell her scary stories so she remembers."
options.then: Ishaan looks unsure. "I don't want to scare her."

options.text: "Only if she's already in some kind of trouble."
options.then: "How would I know?" Ishaan asks.

steps.why: Sharing the numbers spreads real protection to more people.

scenarios.relearn: Knowing your numbers means help is one tap away, for you and others.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Nisha gives her statement in a harassment case tomorrow, and she's very nervous.
scenarios.setup: She calls you late the night before.

steps.prompt: Nisha asks: "Promise me it's a sure thing?"

options.text: "Honestly, I've heard these cases usually fail."
options.then: Nisha goes very quiet on the line.

options.text: "Totally. You'll definitely win this one, trust me on that."
options.then: Nisha relaxes, counting on it completely.

options.text: "I can't promise an outcome. But real, free help exists."
options.then: Nisha sighs. "I know. I just wanted to hear it."

options.text: "Don't think about it now. Just go to sleep, okay?"
options.then: "I can't," she says. "That's the problem."

steps.why: Honesty about outcomes builds trust. A real route is better than a promise.

steps.prompt: Nisha asks: "Should I just say whatever makes them believe me?"

options.text: "Just tell the truth, in your own words. That's enough."
options.then: Nisha breathes out. "Okay. Just the truth."

options.text: "Say whatever you think they most want to hear."
options.then: "I don't know what they want," she says.

options.text: "I'll write you a script tonight, and you can read it out."
options.then: Nisha agrees, then worries it won't sound like her.

options.text: "Add a few extra details, so it sounds stronger."
options.then: Nisha hesitates. "Then I'd have to remember the extra bits."

steps.why: The truth in her own words is enough, and none of this is her fault. Qualified help can guide the rest.

steps.prompt: Nisha says: "Whatever happens, I don't want to feel alone in this."

options.text: "You'll win anyway, so you won't even need me there afterwards."
options.then: "You don't know that," she says softly.

options.text: "If you lose, at least you'll know you really tried."
options.then: Nisha goes quiet. "I hadn't even thought about losing."

options.text: "Call me, but only if it goes badly tomorrow."
options.then: Nisha pauses. "And if it goes well?"

options.text: "You won't be. I'll check in after, whatever the result."
options.then: Nisha laughs a little. "Okay. Bring chocolate."

steps.why: Being there whatever the result is support that doesn't depend on a promise.

scenarios.relearn: Never promise an outcome; offer honesty and a route to real, free help.

scenarios.hook: Your classmate Kavya is being harassed at her summer internship and doesn't know what to do.
scenarios.setup: She tells you at break, keeping her voice low.

steps.prompt: Kavya says: "I'll just keep my head down till it's over."

options.text: "Up to you. But there's an Internal Committee for this."
options.then: Kavya looks up. "A committee? For interns too?"

options.text: "Good idea. Speaking up never changes anything."
options.then: Kavya nods slowly. "Yeah. What's the point?"

options.text: "Are you sure you're not reading too much into it?"
options.then: Kavya's face falls. "I knew I shouldn't have said anything."

options.text: "You have to report it today, or it's on you."
options.then: Kavya looks hurt. "So it's my fault now?"

steps.why: It's never her fault. Respecting her choice while naming the real route gives her options, not pressure.

steps.prompt: Kavya asks: "My cousin says interns can go to a committee. What would I even say?"

options.text: "What happened and when. Writing it down first helps."
options.then: Kavya opens her notes app. "Okay. Monday was the first time."

options.text: "Just say he's creepy. They'll know exactly what you mean."
options.then: Kavya frowns. "Is that enough for them to act?"

options.text: "Nothing yet. Get a video of him doing it first."
options.then: Kavya feels sick at the thought of being alone with him to film.

options.text: "Exaggerate it a bit, so they take it seriously."
options.then: Kavya hesitates. "What if they ask about the parts I added?"

steps.why: A simple record of what happened and when helps the committee understand.

steps.prompt: Kavya says: "I don't want my parents to find out."

options.text: "Then just quit, and tell everyone you got bored of the work."
options.then: Kavya considers it, and the man stays where he is.

options.text: "Then we'll keep it all between the two of us."
options.then: Kavya relaxes, but she still faces him alone each day.

options.text: "Then let's talk to the school counsellor. I'll come too."
options.then: Kavya nods. "Okay. She's easy to talk to."

options.text: "Your parents have to know. I'll tell them tonight."
options.then: Kavya panics. "Please don't. Let me decide."

steps.why: A trusted adult like a counsellor gives her support, while she keeps control.

scenarios.relearn: Workplace harassment has a route: the Internal Committee.
